sourceText: The name on the threshold was WOLFE-NEW-SUN. Beneath it, in smaller letters, was the dedication: Gene Wolfe. It was not a reproduction of a book but a world built around the question the book had made impossible to forget. In the far future, ancient technology is described in ritual vocabulary, and Kesh must infer function without metadata. The memorial bore the name of Gene Wolfe precisely to keep the genealogy of the idea visible. Aster considered it indecent for a late civilization to treat the imagination of the past as anonymous ore: authors did not own the futures, but they deserved to remain on the map as points of intellectual origin. The final period no longer studied worlds but the mechanism by which worlds had become a curriculum. The Table itself had entered the Table, and classification now had to survive criticism without turning into religion. Marae kept her local body vulnerable. Pain, fatigue, and the impossibility of doing ten things at once were epistemic instruments for her, not biological scenery. The children were met by En, who refused demonstrations. ‘If you can perform miracles, perform them after you tell me what becomes 331 irreversible.’ Marae appreciated the formulation; Aster admitted that in earlier eras she herself would have asked the question only after optimizing. The problem closed quickly around them: The mystery delights him, but Aster warns him that ignorance is not automatically depth. There was no clean option. Every intervention shifted the cost between persons, eras, or definitions of personhood; and refusing to intervene was itself a choice made by those who could leave. Kesh opened the analytical layer of the Table for a few seconds. The active cells were At — Artifact as Magic: a late culture uses technology without technical vocabulary; Um — Dying Universe: civilization lives at the end of available energy. Course references included Gene Wolfe; Dying Earth; far future. The rule was strict: naming a work did not substitute for an explanation. They had to identify the mechanism that could migrate into another story and the consequences that could not be copied without remainder. Tern broke the first consensus. ‘Sometimes the ethical question is whether we are entitled to know enough to optimize.’ Kesh answered without raising their voice: ‘If the element explains everything, we do not have an element. We have a word that has eaten the problem.’ It was not a pedagogical quarrel. Over the last nights, the children’s differences had become incompatible political programs. The White Hunger appeared in Aster as a loss of relief. She did not lack entertainment. She lacked the resistance of things to the model. When she could anticipate every reaction, the world became 332 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS functionally an extension of her own mind, and the presence of the other thinned toward simulacrum. Marae remained in the local body when the others opened their protections. The gesture cost her: she felt cold, pressure, and physiological delay at exactly the scale the inhabitants felt them. “Otherwise we risk confusing the fact that we survive with the claim that the situation is bearable,” she said after catching her breath. The night did not end in victory. They find a device that opens exactly the threshold Tern indicated and that does not exist in Aster's designs. Aster recorded the decision in the world’s provenance register and, more importantly, allowed its inhabitants to contest it. For several eras she had been learning something that seems banal to lesser powers: technical reversibility is not the same as biographical reversibility. No one could now claim that Tern was merely pursuing an obsession. The threshold had a technical address, but access required a deliberate reduction of power. The more extensions of Aster one tried to carry through it, the more the channel closed. Exteriority required leaving something behind. For the course, Kesh also linked the night to the EXTERNALIZATION operator. In the Table, periodicity did not mean that the same objects reappeared, but that the same operation — turns an internal property into an object, companion, infrastructure, or institution — could recur across different families. Thus a copy of a body, a copy of a mind, a copy of a world, and a copy 333 of a history were not the same phenomenon, but they shared a conceptual chemistry. Vela introduced the propagation test: if you remove the speculative idea and nothing in the institutions, relationships, or vocabulary has to be rewritten, the idea has remained scenery. Kesh introduced the opposite test: if the idea seems to explain every detail, you have overcompressed the world. Between the two tests lay the region in which an element became fertile without becoming superstition. Marae added the refusal test. Who can say “no,” and what happens afterward? In universes with near-divine technology, that question often separated an instrument from a regime. A power that treats refusal as a data error can be benevolent in intention and totalitarian in structure. They left without an oral summary. Aster had abandoned the habit of closing every night with a thesis; some worlds were more honestly preserved as problems than as lessons. 334 THE PERIODIC TABLE OF SPECULATIVE IDEAS
